Electrolyte-Rich Solution

Vitamins

Vitamin B1 (Thiamine)

A water-soluble vitamin that the body converts into an active coenzyme needed to break down glucose for energy. This process takes place in the mitochondria, the energy-producing structures within our cells. Tissues with high energy demands such as the brain, nerves and heart are particularly reliant on it. The body stores very little thiamine so a regular supply is needed. It contributes to normal energy-yielding metabolism, the normal functioning of the nervous system and the normal function of the heart.

Vitamin B2 (Riboflavin)

A water-soluble vitamin that the body uses to make coenzymes needed by the mitochondria to produce energy. It also helps recycle glutathione, one of the body's main antioxidants, so it can continue protecting cells. It contributes to normal energy-yielding metabolism, the maintenance of normal skin, the protection of cells from oxidative stress and the reduction of tiredness and fatigue.

Vitamin B3 (Niacin)

A water-soluble vitamin that the body uses to make NAD, one of the most important coenzymes in the body. NAD is involved in hundreds of reactions that convert food into cellular energy and help repair and maintain cells. It contributes to normal energy-yielding metabolism, normal psychological function, the maintenance of normal skin and the reduction of tiredness and fatigue.

Vitamin B5 (Pantothenic Acid)

A water-soluble vitamin that the body uses to make coenzyme A, a molecule at the centre of metabolism. Coenzyme A is needed to release energy from carbohydrates, fats and proteins and to produce certain hormones. It contributes to normal energy-yielding metabolism, normal mental performance, the normal synthesis of steroid hormones and some neurotransmitters and the reduction of tiredness and fatigue.

Vitamin B6 (Pyridoxine)

A water-soluble vitamin that is converted into an active coenzyme used by more than 100 enzymes, most of them involved in protein metabolism. It is needed to produce neurotransmitters (chemical messengers that carry signals between nerve cells) such as serotonin and dopamine, and to form haemoglobin, the protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen. It contributes to normal red blood cell formation, the normal function of the immune system and the regulation of hormonal activity.

Vitamin B12 (Cobalamin)

A water-soluble vitamin that works alongside folate in the production of DNA and in the formation of healthy red blood cells. It also plays a role in maintaining the protective coating around nerve fibres. As the body relies on a complex process to absorb it from the gut, some people find it difficult to maintain healthy levels. It contributes to normal red blood cell formation, the normal function of the immune system and nervous system, normal energy-yielding metabolism and the reduction of tiredness and fatigue.

Biotin (Vitamin B7)

A water-soluble vitamin that acts as a coenzyme for enzymes involved in the metabolism of fats, carbohydrates and amino acids. These reactions support energy production and the building of fatty acids, which the skin relies on to maintain its natural protective barrier. Biotin is closely linked to the health of hair, skin and nails, and a lack of biotin is known to cause hair thinning, brittle nails and skin rashes. It contributes to the maintenance of normal hair and normal skin, normal energy-yielding metabolism and the normal metabolism of macronutrients.

Used in

Folic Acid (Vitamin B9)

The synthetic form of folate. Once converted into its active form it supplies the building blocks needed to make DNA, which makes it essential in tissues where cells divide rapidly. It works alongside vitamin B12 in several key metabolic processes. It contributes to normal blood formation, the normal function of the immune system, the process of cell division and the reduction of tiredness and fatigue.

Used in

  • Hair & Scalp Pro Infusion
  • Energy Infusion
Vitamin C (Ascorbic Acid)

A water-soluble antioxidant that humans cannot produce and must obtain from their diet. It is needed by the enzymes that build and stabilise collagen, the main structural protein in skin and blood vessels. It neutralises free radicals and is found in high concentrations in white blood cells. It contributes to the normal function of the immune system, normal collagen formation for the normal function of the skin, the protection of cells from oxidative stress and the reduction of tiredness and fatigue. Intravenous delivery bypasses the limits of gut absorption and achieves blood levels many times higher than oral supplements.

Vitamin D

A fat-soluble vitamin that the body makes in the skin when it is exposed to sunlight. In the UK we don't get enough sunlight, especially in the winter months, which makes deficiency one of the most common nutrient deficiencies in the country. Vitamin D is essential for the body to absorb calcium and phosphorus from food. It contributes to the maintenance of normal bones, teeth and muscle function and to the normal function of the immune system. Low levels are associated with tiredness, low mood, muscle aches and bone pain, and over time can weaken the bones. People who spend little time outdoors, cover their skin or have darker skin are at particular risk.

Minerals

Magnesium

An essential mineral that is needed by more than 300 enzymes in the body. It is required to activate ATP, the molecule cells use to store and transfer energy. It also regulates the movement of calcium and potassium in and out of cells, which is central to muscle contraction and nerve signalling. It contributes to the reduction of tiredness and fatigue, electrolyte balance, normal muscle function and the normal functioning of the nervous system.

  • Recovery Pro Infusion
  • Myers Cocktail Infusion
Zinc

An essential trace mineral required for the activity of more than 300 enzymes. It is needed for the development and function of immune cells and for making DNA and new proteins. Because the body has no dedicated store of zinc a regular supply is important. It contributes to the normal function of the immune system, normal protein synthesis, the maintenance of normal hair, skin and nails and the protection of cells from oxidative stress.

Selenium

An essential trace mineral that the body builds into a group of proteins called selenoproteins. These include glutathione peroxidase, a key antioxidant enzyme that neutralises harmful molecules, and the enzymes that activate thyroid hormone. It contributes to the normal function of the immune system, the protection of cells from oxidative stress, normal thyroid function and the maintenance of normal hair and nails.

Amino Acids

Glutamine

The most abundant amino acid in the blood and muscle. It is considered conditionally essential because the body's needs can exceed what it can make during intense exercise, illness or stress. It is an important fuel for cells of the immune system and the lining of the gut, and it plays a role in maintaining muscle protein.

Used in

  • Muscle & Fitness Infusion
L-Leucine

An essential branched-chain amino acid and one of the most important for muscle. It acts as a key signal that switches on muscle protein synthesis, the process the body uses to build and repair muscle tissue.

Used in

  • Muscle & Fitness Infusion
L-Valine

An essential branched-chain amino acid that works alongside leucine and isoleucine. It is used to build muscle protein and can be used by muscle as a source of energy during prolonged exercise.

Used in

  • Muscle & Fitness Infusion
Isoleucine

An essential branched-chain amino acid found in high concentrations in muscle. It is used to build proteins, can be broken down within muscle for energy during exercise and is involved in the uptake of glucose into muscle cells.

L-Phenylalanine

An essential amino acid used to build proteins. The body also converts it into tyrosine, which is needed to make dopamine, noradrenaline and adrenaline.

Used in

Lysine

An essential amino acid, meaning the body cannot make it and it must come from the diet. It is a building block of proteins and has a particular role in collagen, where it helps give the protein its strength and stability. The body also uses lysine to make carnitine.

Arginine

An amino acid used to build proteins and to help the body clear nitrogen waste. It is also the starting material for nitric oxide, a molecule that relaxes the walls of blood vessels and helps regulate blood flow.

Taurine

A sulphur-containing amino acid found in high concentrations in the heart, muscles, brain and eyes. Unlike most amino acids it is not used to build proteins. Instead it helps regulate hydration within cells and the movement of calcium, which is important for muscle contraction. In the liver it also helps form bile, which aids the digestion of fats.

Carnitine

A compound made in the body from the amino acids lysine and methionine, most of which is stored in muscle. Its main role is to transport fatty acids into the mitochondria, where they are broken down to produce energy. This makes it central to how the body uses fat as a fuel source.

Antioxidants and Coenzymes

Glutathione

Glutathione is often described as the body's most powerful antioxidant. It is made naturally from three amino acids: glutamic acid, cysteine and glycine. Most of it is produced in the liver, although almost every cell in the body makes its own supply. It neutralises free radicals, the unstable molecules that damage cells. Because oxidative stress is closely linked to inflammation, glutathione also helps regulate the body's inflammatory response. For the skin it protects cells from the oxidative stress caused by UV exposure and pollution, and it acts on the enzyme that controls pigmentation, which contributes to a brighter and more even complexion. Levels decline with age and can be depleted by alcohol, illness and oxidative stress. An infusion delivers glutathione directly into the bloodstream to boost your levels. Its effects have made it one of the most popular ingredients in the health, wellness and beauty industry.

  • Beauty & Glow Infusion

NAD+ (Nicotinamide Adenine Dinucleotide)

A coenzyme found in every cell of the body and essential for energy production. It works inside the mitochondria, the tiny structures within each cell that turn nutrients into usable energy. It is also needed by the enzymes that repair damaged DNA and help keep cells healthy. Levels of NAD+ fall naturally as we age and can also be depleted by stress, illness and alcohol. Research has linked this decline to lower cellular energy and a reduced ability to repair DNA. These changes contribute to common signs of ageing such as fatigue, reduced mental clarity and changes in the skin. Skin cells rely on NAD+ to produce the energy needed for renewal and to repair DNA damage caused by UV exposure. NAD+ has become one of the most popular treatments in wellness and longevity medicine, with people choosing it to support their energy levels, mental clarity, cellular repair and healthy ageing. Our NAD+ is sourced from a UK-registered supplier and each batch is supplied with a certificate of analysis confirming its quality and sterility.

Used in

  • NAD+ Infusion
  • Longevity Infusion
Coenzyme Q10 (CoQ10)

A compound made naturally in the body and found in the mitochondria of almost every cell. It is most concentrated in organs with the highest energy demands, such as the heart, liver, kidneys and muscles. CoQ10 plays an essential role in the final stage of energy production, where it helps convert nutrients into ATP, the cell's energy source. It is also one of the few antioxidants the body makes itself that works within cell membranes, where it protects cells from damage and helps regenerate vitamin E. The body's production of CoQ10 begins to fall from early adulthood and levels can also be lowered by certain medications such as statins. Because it is fat-soluble, CoQ10 can be poorly absorbed when taken as a supplement. We have included it in our menu for those who want extra support for cellular energy and antioxidant protection, particularly as they get older.

Used in

Iron

Monofer (Ferric Derisomaltose)

An intravenous iron formulation in which iron is tightly bound within a carbohydrate structure. This allows iron to be released steadily, so a large dose can be given in a single infusion. Once in the bloodstream the iron is taken up by the body's stores, where it replenishes ferritin and is used to produce haemoglobin.

Standalone Infusions & Injections

Alpha Lipoic Acid (ALA)

An antioxidant made in small amounts in the mitochondria, where it helps the enzymes that convert glucose into energy. It is unique because it works in both the watery and fatty parts of the cell, so it can act in places many other antioxidants cannot reach. ALA is sometimes called the antioxidant of antioxidants because it helps regenerate others, including vitamin C, vitamin E, glutathione and CoQ10, extending their protective effect. It has also been studied for its role in supporting healthy nerve function and the way the body uses glucose. We have included ALA in our menu as a versatile antioxidant that complements many of our infusions, particularly those focused on energy, detox and healthy ageing.
